name: Arena-score nowcasting: simulate the pairwise-vote mechanism that settles the monthly 'best AI model' markets
one_line: Run your own judge-model pairwise battles between a new release and the incumbents, fit Bradley-Terry with the leaderboard's own uncertainty, and price where a low-vote Arena score will converge by the monthly snapshot.
scope: Cover the recurring 'Which company has the best AI model end of <month>?' family. Rules fetched today: the market resolves on the arena.ai Text Arena Overall board with style control OFF, checked at 12:00 ET on the last day of the month. Rank decides, ties go to Arena score, and AutoEval-marked models are excluded. The file needs two layers. (1) Statistics only: turn the published score, CI and vote count into P(rank flip by snapshot) as votes accumulate. New entrants sit near 5k votes at +/-8-9, while incumbents sit at 40-75k votes at +/-3-4. (2) Simulated votes: a cross-family judge panel battles the new model against incumbents on an Arena-like prompt mix. Length and markdown preference must be reproduced, not removed, because the market uses the no-style-control board. The output is a forecast of the converged score before the leaderboard has enough votes. Add release-calendar OSINT, the lab private-testing selection effect, and vote rigging as a manipulation risk on the resolution source. State plainly that whether specialist traders already do this is unverified. Boundaries: enumerable human panels stay in critic-pool-panel-twins. Release-date markets are out of scope.
why_it_matters: This is the one place where an LLM simulation has a validated correlation above 0.9 with the exact statistic that settles a liquid, recurring market. Arena-Hard-Auto reports 98.6% correlation with Arena human-preference rankings for about $20 a run [pre-2025, possibly stale]. Length-controlled AlpacaEval reaches Spearman 0.98 [pre-2025, possibly stale]. The September 2026 event has $3.63M volume and $1.45M liquidity, with Anthropic at 0.9855. The October event already shows $352k volume and $679k liquidity across 21 company markets. Live board, updated 2026-09-13: #1 is at 1508 +/-8 on 5,783 votes, and a Google entrant is at 1495 +/-9 on 5,076 votes. The race sits inside the CI, so the edge is the convergence forecast. Twelve or more resolutions a year give statistical power that the list's one-off events lack. Cheap validation: run a retro on the last 10-15 frontier releases, comparing a judge-BT prediction from release-day API access against the score at 30k votes. Then log daily board snapshots against prices for three monthly cycles.
flags: Never submit Arena votes on a market you hold. Vote rigging with a few hundred votes is documented and would be manipulation of the resolution source. Lab staff hold MNPI on releases and private Arena tests. Judge self-preference bias needs a cross-family panel. Tech category taker feeRate is 0.04, so prefer maker expression. The top rank is structurally fragile: one paper reports 92% top-1 swaps on held-out splits.
